title: Non for Profit Salary Packaging: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using our 38-hour week calculator. Includes non for profit salary packaging, tax, super, and award rates for Australian workers.
salarySummary: Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, giving annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: What is non for profit salary packaging?
faqs.a: It is a tax-effective arrangement where employees of eligible not-for-profit organisations can salary package up to $15,900 per year for general living expenses, reducing their taxable income. This is not included in our calculator but can significantly affect take-home pay.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate as compensation for not receiving paid leave. Our calculator has a checkbox to add this loading automatically.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you receive an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to understand what that means over a full year. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a typical full-time employee, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives you an annual gross figure before tax, super, and any salary packaging.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Using the formula: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year. If you are a casual employee, the 25% loading brings the rate to $33.05 per hour, and the annual figure becomes $65,336.80. These calculations also help you see your fortnightly pay: simply double your weekly amount.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. Award rates are specific to your job classification and industry, and they include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime provisions. Our calculator uses the base hourly rate you enter; it does not automatically apply award conditions. If you are covered by an award, check the relevant pay guide for your exact rate.

Casual loading is a separate addition. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add this loading. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading; let the calculator apply it correctly.

## Average Weekly Earnings: A Broader Picture

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) figures. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary-time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. All employees (including part-time) earned $1,579.20 per week on average. These are averages, not medians, and they represent the whole workforce, not your specific job. Use them as a benchmark, not a target.

## Tax and Medicare in 2026–27

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. This is an estimate only.

For the National Minimum Wage example ($52,269.44), tax would be approximately $6,200 and Medicare $1,045, leaving a take-home of about $45,023. Your actual tax may differ if you have deductions, offsets, or salary packaging.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. For the NMW example, super would be $6,272.33 per year. Our calculator shows this as an estimate.

## Non for Profit Salary Packaging

If you work for an eligible not-for-profit organisation, you can access salary packaging – also called salary sacrifice. This allows you to pay for certain expenses with pre-tax dollars, reducing your taxable income. The most common benefit is the ability to package up to $15,900 per year for general living expenses (such as rent, mortgage, or bills), plus up to $2,650 for meal entertainment. This can significantly increase your take-home pay.

For example, if your annual gross is $52,269 and you salary package $15,900, your taxable income drops to $36,369. You would then pay less tax and Medicare. Our calculator does not include salary packaging, but you can use the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to learn more about how it works.

## Putting It All Together

To get a complete picture of your annual pay, start with your hourly rate and the 38-hour week formula. Then consider whether you are casual (add loading), check your award rate, and factor in tax and super. If you work in the non for profit sector, explore salary packaging as a way to boost your take-home pay.

Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, including tax and super estimates. Remember, this is an estimate – not a determination of your actual pay. For precise advice, consult your employer, a tax professional, or the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
